commonNameFr.name: Crapaud du Grand Bassin
commonNameFr.source: NatureServe Explorer (French common names listed: 'Crapaud du Grand Bassin', 'Crapaud pied-bêche du Grand Bassin', 'Pied-bêche du Grand Bassin')

taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes inconsistency in older literature among S. hammondii, S. intermontana and S. multiplicata (hammondii and multiplicata were once treated as conspecific).
fieldMarks: Gray, olive or brown back mottled with darker spots that have light centres, with gray streaks outlining an hourglass-shaped mark; underside light gray to cream and unmarked.
Large, catlike golden-yellow eyes with vertical pupils; a dark brown or orange spot on each upper eyelid; nose slightly upturned with a raised callus between the eyes.
Black keratinized spade on the underside of each hind foot; body short and fat with stubby limbs, 32-67 mm long.
Skin is relatively smooth with small bumps and no parotoid glands, unlike true toads (Bufo).
Male call: monotonous duck-like snoring of 1-3 notes, carrying over long distances.
behavior: Mostly nocturnal but also active early morning and late afternoon; more active after rain and in humid periods.
Survives dry country by burrowing with its hind-foot spades or using rodent burrows; daytime burrows are shallow, typically 35-45 cm deep, deeper when drier.
Explosive breeder, May-August, at still or slow water; adults migrate 1-5 km at night; pools must hold water about 40 days for tadpoles to transform.
Generalist insectivore; ants and darkling beetles are the commonest prey.
habitat: Arid regions: sagebrush flats, semi-desert shrubland, alkali flats and pinyon-juniper, up to ponderosa pine and spruce-fir near 2,800 m, wherever soils are loose enough to burrow.
Breeds in temporary or permanent still water such as seasonal pools, springs, irrigation ditches and ponds.
range: Southern British Columbia south through central and eastern Washington and Oregon, southern Idaho, eastern California, Nevada, Utah, Wyoming and northwestern Colorado to northwestern Arizona, from the Cascade-Sierra axis east to the Rockies.

lookalikes.name: Plains spadefoot (Spea bombifrons)
lookalikes.howToTell: Separated mainly by range; plains spadefoot has a hard boss between the eyes, a four-line hourglass marking and a brief snore call.
